subject: EdgeLocker private cluster: fleet sizing, NIC segmentation, and block-store lifecycle
messages:
From: Ben Martin <ben@airlock-systems.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Chen <alice@airlock-systems.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0400
Subject: Private deployment kickoff: AirLock site inventory + topology (EdgeLocker)

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for taking time. We're in prep for deploying EdgeLocker (on-prem private deployment) into two pilot sites later this quarter and want to lock down cluster sizing, network zoning (NIC segmentation), and PV lifecycle/retention expectations before the preflight. High level:

- Two sites (NYC1, ORD2), each ~12 racks.
- Each site needs 3 control-plane nodes + dedicated inference pools (mixed A100/RTX), and smaller infra pools for logging/metrics.
- Network ops require strict NIC segmentation: management plane, inference data ingress, customer-facing egress.
- Storage: mix of local NVMe for KV/cache, and central NAS-backed blockstore for persistent model artifacts and traces. Need guidance on PVC class choices and retention policies for model checkpoints and audit logs.

I've attached our current site inventory and a rough network diagram. Can you propose an initial fleet/node-profile plan and the PVC strategy you expect Redwood to recommend (reclaim policies, snapshot cadence, backup targets)? If there's anything missing in our inventory, tell us what to collect.

Attachments: airlock_site_inventory.xlsx, airlock_network_diagram.png

Best,
Ben

Ben — thanks for the inventory and diagram. High-level reaction and ask below; attaching a concise node-profile suggestion so we can iterate quickly.

Quick replies to your bullets:
- Control plane: 3 dedicated CP nodes per site is correct (HA + maintenance headroom). Plan for CP nodes on separate failure domains (two racks + maintenance spare).
- Inference pools: we'll propose two inference tiers: "high-throughput" (dense A100s, shared KV cache) and "burst/low-latency" (RTXs with local NVMe). We'll specify instance counts per site in the attachment.
- NIC segmentation: must gate management traffic (k8s API, kubelet) into a dedicated management VLAN/subnet with source-restricted access (Bastion + mgmt firewall rules). Inference data ingress should be on a separate high-throughput VLAN; egress to customers on an egress VLAN with SNAT and monitored egress proxies.
- Storage: recommended approach in brief: local NVMe for ephemerally cached KV; RWO block PVs on network blockstore for model artifacts; an object store endpoint (S3-compatible) for long-term checkpoints and traces. We'll call out snapshot cadence and retention per PVC class in the matrix.

Missing items that'd help us size properly:
- Typical request concurrency / peak tokens/sec per site (estimate).
- Model sizes (parameter counts) and working-set expectations for KV cache.
- RPO/RTO targets for model artifacts and audit log retention windows.

Next steps: Marissa will drive contractual SOW items; Soojin and Vivek will provide technical node profiles and storage lifecycle recommendations. Can the AirLock ops team join a 60-minute preflight on Oct 13? If that works, we can lock the draft fleet plan beforehand.

Attachments: redwood_node_profile_suggestion.xlsx

Cheers,

Subject: Re: Private deployment kickoff: AirLock site inventory + topology (EdgeLocker)

Ben / team — adding technical detail inline and attaching the PV retention matrix. Long email, tl;dr at top.

TL;DR (recommendations):
- Node classes: CP (3x m64-32g), infra (2-3 x m16-64g), inference-high-throughput (A100: 8 GPUs/node, 6 nodes/site), inference-low-latency (RTX6000: 2 GPUs/node, 8 nodes/site). Add a 10% spare buffer for rolling updates.
- Networking: management VLAN (10.10.0.0/24), data-in VLAN (10.20.0.0/22) with jumbo frames, egress VLAN (10.30.0.0/24) with egress proxies and NAT. Use MAC + IP ACLs on top-of-rack switches to restrict cross-VLAN lateral movement for management plane.
- Storage classes:
  - sc-local-nvme (StorageClass: local-static, capacity: provisioned per-node) — for KV/shard cache (no snapshots, ephemeral, recreate on pod reschedule); use nodeAffinity.
  - sc-blockstore-fast (RBD/iSCSI backed) — RWO, snapshots daily, retain 7 days; for model artifacts under active development.
  - sc-blockstore-archive (object+hns) — for long-term checkpoints and audit logs; lifecycle to object store with 30d warm retention then transition to archive.

PVC & retention rules (from attached pv_retention_matrix.csv):
- model-checkpoint: 7d snapshot, 30d object copy, GC at 90d unless flagged for long-term.
- audit-logs: write-to-object immediately, keep hot copies for 14d in blockstore then archive.

Operational notes:
- KV cache: design for hot working-set to fit per-node NVMe cache; we recommend global prefix caching on Redis-compatible layer optionally colocated on infra nodes.
- Backups: snapshots of blockstore to an on-site object gateway then replicate to the other site nightly. DR runbooks will use the latest replicated snapshot.
- Quotas: enforce PVC quotas per namespace and token-level cost attribution via Redwood Console integration.

Attachments: pv_retention_matrix.csv

1) For sc-blockstore-fast snapshots (daily, retain 7d) — is the snapshotting mechanism dependent on a particular CSI driver? We run Ceph RBD at both sites.
2) For the NVMe local caches: if a node fails, what's the recommended approach for cache warmup so we don't see cold starts across the cluster?

We're good to confirm Oct 13 10:00am EDT for the preflight — I'll send a calendar invite and include our ops/NetEng folks. If you want an updated site inventory after we've reconciled serials, I'll attach it to the invite.

Also, what's the SOW cadence for final node counts (do we need a signed SOW prior to procurement)? Marissa — looping you for SOW and order process.
